title: Russell US Style indexes — conditional MONTH-end recapping effective at the open (24% / 4.8%-above-48% test struck on the 2026-11-24 close), the last check before the December quarter-end instance
source: EST: owner-published, read direct this session. FTSE Russell, "Capping Methodology Guide", v5.4, September 2026 (lseg.com dam policy-documents, capping-methodology-guide.pdf, HTTP 200, 652,008 bytes, 62 content streams inflated 2026-09-08). Its section 4.8.6 table -- "The indices subject to additional capping checks, together with the applicable schedules, trigger thresholds and recapping methodologies" -- carries every Russell US Style index (Russell 1000 Value/Growth, Russell Top 200 Value/Growth, Russell Midcap Value/Growth, Russell 3000/3000E Value/Growth, Russell Top 500, Russell 2500, Russell 2000, Russell Small Cap, Russell Microcap) with frequency "Monthly", price date "T-3", effective date "Last business day of each month", trigger "No company is greater than 24%, and all companies that have a weight greater than 4.8% in aggregate are no more than 48% of the index", scheme "Rule 4.2/RIC 22.5/45". CORROBORATED IN A SECOND, INDEPENDENTLY ARCHIVED EDITION: v5.3, August 2026, recovered from web.archive.org (snapshot 2026-09-02) and inflated in-session, carries the identical "Monthly" / "Last business day of each month" wording for the same rows. THE DATE IS ARITHMETIC FROM THE STANDING RULE, NOT A PUBLISHED CALENDAR ENTRY: the last business day of November 2026 is Monday 30 November, so the effective date is 2026-11-30 and T-3 is Tuesday 2026-11-24 (T-1 Fri 27 Nov, T-2 Wed 25 Nov, stepping over Thanksgiving Thu 26 Nov). Filed estimate on four counts, one of which is a genuine conflict a later lane must not read as settled: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for an index owner's published methodology; this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep; the date is derived from a standing rule rather than read off the owner's dated schedule table, which publishes only the four quarter-end instances; and THE OWNER'S OWN JULY 2026 FAQ CONTRADICTS THE GUIDE, saying verbatim "The review is conducted quarterly (March, June, September, and December)". Conditional by construction -- "If no breach is identified, no changes are made." Discovered during the russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-12-31 initial research, checked 2026-09-08
notes: PROPOSED by the russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-12-31 initial research (2026-09-08). WHY A LANE RESEARCHING A DECEMBER EVENT IS FILING A NOVEMBER ONE: the December instance's own research had to establish what the check's frequency actually is, and found that the calendar's whole model of this family -- four quarter-end instances a year -- comes from a July 2026 FAQ the owner's methodology guide superseded. Between the June 2026 (v5.2) and August 2026 (v5.3) editions of the Capping Methodology Guide, every Russell US Style row in the section 4.8.6 table changed from "Last business day in Mar, Jun, Sep and Dec" to frequency "Monthly" / "Last business day of each month". v5.2's wording is what the sibling ledger russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-09-30 recorded, and it also misattributed it -- the quarterly wording that survives in v5.4 belongs to the two FTSE Emerging ex China rows two lines above the Russell ones. If the guide governs, this family runs TWELVE conditional recapping checks a year on about $294.6B of iShares assets (IWF, IWD, IWY, IWX, IWP, IWS, IWO, IWN) and the calendar tracks four. THIS INSTANCE SPECIFICALLY, rather than all eight untracked ones: 2026-11-30 is the last check before the 2026-12-28 quarter-end strike, so it is the one whose outcome a December-lane pulse would actually have to read. Its October sibling was filed alongside it (proposals/russell-style-month-end-capping-effective-2026-10-30.from-russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-12-31.json); the 2027 instances were DELIBERATELY DECLINED because no owner document published this session names a 2027 date and a standing-rule extrapolation twelve months out is calendar noise, not foresight. WHAT THE PROPOSING RESEARCH'S VERDICT WAS, travelling with the proposal so nobody sizes this as tradable: stand aside. The measured breach probability for a comparable window is single-digit -- from a 45% reset the cohort must beat its own index by 6.67%, which cleared 111 of 1,237 rolling 17-session windows (8.97%, IWF cohort) and 96 of 1,237 (7.76%, IWY cohort) across five years of real prices; the November instance's own drift window from the 2026-10-27 October T-3 is 20 sessions, in the same band. The single-name leg is dead by a wide margin (NVDA 16.21% in IWY against a 24% trigger), five of the eight funds carry no constituent within reach of 4.8% at all, and a fired recap moves about 3pp of IWY's $15.94B -- roughly $478M -- across five of the most liquid names on the tape. Impact low and symbols deliberately EMPTY on the same measured grounds as both quarter-end entries. Kind sector matches the family. A RESEARCHING LANE'S FIRST JOB IS THE CONFLICT, NOT THE ARITHMETIC: if FTSE Russell has published an index notice, a FAQ revision, or a guide version past v5.4 that restores quarterly wording for the Russell US Style rows, this entry and its October sibling should be withdrawn rather than researched.
